mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to a tightening monetary policy by the Fed, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases do not correlate with subsequent Fed tightening actions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the last three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of falling unemployment (t-test p > 0.05), or UNRATE decreases do not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals increased demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases do not correlate with broader economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy in an inflationary environment, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent negative market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing nonfarm payrolls (t-test p > 0.05), or PAYEMS increases do not correlate with improved economic conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decreases do not correlate with subsequent negative market performance.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same period, it signals a strong consumer-driven economy, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of increasing RSAFS and decreasing UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent positive market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month signals an immediate easing of monetary policy, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decreases do not correlate with subsequent positive market performance.
